Encode Coordinates as Open Location Codes (Google Plus Codes)

Source: R/vantor_fieldwork.R
vantor_plus_code.Rd

Converts WGS84 longitude and latitude coordinates into 10- or 11-character Open Location Codes (Plus Codes) (e.g., "85FQPPV4+2V"). Plus Codes are an open, offline-capable alphanumeric street address standard supported by Google Maps, ODK Collect, and field navigation apps without requiring an internet connection.

Usage

vantor_plus_code(lon, lat, code_length = 10L)

Arguments

lon

Numeric vector of longitudes in decimal degrees (-180 to 180).

lat

Numeric vector of latitudes in decimal degrees (-90 to 90).

code_length

Integer. Number of significant characters in the Plus Code (10 for ~14 x 14 m precision, 11 for ~3 x 3 m building-level precision). Default is 10L.

Value

A character vector of formatted Plus Codes (with a "+" separator after the 8th character).

Examples

# Encode coordinates in downtown Denver, CO
vantor_plus_code(lon = -104.995, lat = 39.740)
#> [1] "85FQP2R4+22"
